## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

At head `4d381bcc`, the Quick Notes overlay does not open. The shell rejects the new plugin manifest, so the keybinding, the bar indicator and the "Take a note" menu row do nothing. Only the `omarchy-notes` CLI works. Once the manifest loads, a few paths in the overlay can overwrite or drop note text. The findings below are ordered by impact.

### The Notes plugin manifest is rejected, so the overlay never opens

`shell/plugins/notes/manifest.json` has no `version` field. `PluginRegistry.validateManifest` requires `id`, `name`, `version`, `kinds` and `entryPoints` (`shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml:52-57`) and applies this check to first-party plugins too. Every other first-party manifest has `version`.

```text
Super+Ctrl+M / bar icon / menu "Take a note"
  -> omarchy-notes -i
  -> omarchy-shell shell summon omarchy.notes
  -> shell.summon: plugin not registered -> "unknown"   (overlay never created)
```

`test/shell.d/plugins-test.sh` passes on the merge-base and fails at head with a single error: `omarchy.notes must have version`. When the shell's own validator runs over all first-party manifests, it accepts 37 of 37 on the merge-base, and at head it rejects only `notes/manifest.json`. Current `quattro` doesn't change this.

**Impact:** None of the three new entry points opens the overlay. Each one fails silently.

**Suggested change:** Add `"version": "1.0.0"` (and `"author"`, as `reminders/manifest.json` has). The other required fields already pass validation.

### Loading the note can overwrite or misplace text that is being typed

`NotesFlow.open()` always starts `omarchy-notes --read` and focuses the editor right away. When the read finishes, it unconditionally assigns `noteTextEdit.text = text`.

| Situation | Result (from source, not observed in a running shell) |
|---|---|
| Shortcut pressed again while the overlay is open | `summon` calls `open()` again, and typing since the first open is replaced by the saved file |
| Typing or `Esc` before the first read finishes | Typed characters are replaced; `Esc` saves the editor's current content, which is empty on the first open after a shell start |
| First open after a shell start | Qt places the cursor at position 0 after replacing the text, so new text is inserted before the existing note (`Buy milk` + typed `Call mom` saves `Call momBuy milk`) |

`close()` (reached through `shell hide`) sets `opened = false` without saving, so changing the binding to `toggle` would not preserve the text either.

**Impact:** Unsaved typing can be lost, or the new text can be merged into the start of the existing note. How often the read finishes after typing begins was not measured.

**Suggested change:** Skip the reload in `open()` when the overlay is already open. Ignore a read result once the editor has been edited, or keep editing disabled until the read completes. Move the cursor to the end after loading (`noteTextEdit.cursorPosition = noteTextEdit.length`). Save on `close()` as well.

### Overlay saves go through one command-line argument, and failures are not reported

`submit()` runs `Quickshell.execDetached(["omarchy-notes", noteTextEdit.text])` and then closes the overlay unconditionally. `execDetached` does not report whether the process started (Quickshell v0.3.1, `src/core/qmlglobal.cpp`).

| Note text (synthetic, run in a private `HOME`) | Result |
|---|---|
| Exactly `-i`, `--interactive`, `--read`, `-h` or `--help` | Parsed as an option; not saved, and the previous note is kept |
| `- [ ] todo`, `--not-a-flag` | Saved verbatim |
| 131071 bytes | Saved |
| 131072 bytes or more | Exec fails with `E2BIG`; the file is unchanged and the overlay still closes |

**Impact:** In these cases the overlay closes as if the note were saved, and the edits are gone.

**Suggested change:** Pass the text on stdin through a dedicated write mode (for example `omarchy-notes --write`, fed from a `Process` with `stdinEnabled`). Keep the overlay open, or show an error, when the process exits non-zero. Writing to a temporary file in the same directory and renaming it over the note also removes the truncate-then-write window in `printf ... > "$NOTES_FILE"`.

### The CLI replaces the whole note

**Verified:** `omarchy-notes "text"` writes the note byte-for-byte, with no shell evaluation of `$(...)`, backticks or backslashes, and `--read` returns it unchanged.

Each call replaces the entire file, though. `omarchy-notes "Buy milk"` followed by `omarchy-notes "Call mom"` leaves only `Call mom`, including anything typed in the overlay. Unquoted `omarchy-notes Buy milk` saves only `Buy`, exits 0 and discards the previous note.

**Impact:** A CLI call silently replaces the existing note, including text saved from the overlay. An unquoted multi-word call keeps only the first word and still reports success.

**Suggested change:** Use `"$*"`. If the CLI is meant for quickly jotting a thought, consider appending a line rather than replacing the note.

### Integration notes

- **Menu aliases:** `trigger.notes` and `trigger.notes.take` declare `aliases`. `AGENTS.md` says not to add aliases to new menu entries.
- **Open notes file:** `xdg-open ~/Documents/Notes/QuickNotes.md` fails silently until a note has been saved, because `omarchy-notes -i` does not create the file. Other file-opening rows use `omarchy-launch-editor`.
- **Menu order:** The Notes rows are declared among the Reminder rows but render as the last Trigger row.
- **Bar settings:** `Indicators.manifest.json` does not list Notes among the selectable indicators, so it can't be picked in the bar settings once a custom list is set.
- **Discoverability:** `bin/omarchy` has no `GROUP_DESCRIPTIONS[notes]` entry, so bare `omarchy` lists `reminder` but not `notes`. `manual/07-hotkeys.md` doesn't list `Super + Ctrl + M`.
- **Indicator role:** The indicator is always inactive (`active: false`), so it appears only on hover or with always-show. Other indicators reflect a state. Whether a stateless launcher belongs in the Indicators group is a maintainer decision.

**Verified:** `Super + Ctrl + M` doesn't conflict with any other binding at head or on current `quattro`. The menu JSONC parses, and the new routes resolve. The menu, binding-conflict and keybindings-menu tests pass at head. `TextEdit` defaults to plain text, so note text that looks like HTML is not reinterpreted.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head against its merge-base and current `quattro`, including Quickshell v0.3.1 and Qt 6.11.2 source (Omarchy doesn't pin a version). Selected repository tests, a manifest-validation check and the `omarchy-notes` CLI ran in an isolated sandbox with a synthetic home directory. Node-based tests ran under a Node-compatible runtime. No desktop session was used: the overlay was not opened, and the timing and cursor behavior above come from source reading.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, with targeted follow-up questions to resolve disagreements, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
